description: The study records simulator responses to road-marking and pavement treatments at rural curves and pedestrian crossings. The University of Zagreb describes 94 recruited drivers and collection from 10 March to 16 April 2026. SILAB represents Croatian road geometry with a 20.82 km recorded experimental section, ten curves and eight crossings, using five counterbalanced scenarios. Per-drive CSV files sample approximately 60 Hz and include steering, pedals, speed, acceleration, network identifiers and lane position. This is simulated behaviour, not observed on-road driving. The source states pseudonymisation; participant records and values were not inspected. Actual usable-drive count and missing samples remain unknown. The named source creators provide this metadata through Zenodo, whose deposits declare CC BY 4.0. Access restrictions and underlying provider terms remain separate from that declaration; cost is unknown unless explicitly stated. Geographic and temporal coverage are limited to the source-described roads, scenarios or periods. Metadata only was reviewed, with no files, measurements, imagery, archives or document bodies downloaded. Related components retain their distinct native identities and possible overlap. The described physical assets, observations or simulator outputs support road infrastructure simulation within these stated limits.
